subject.title: [Bug] Orphaned/oversized native Codex thread wedges a session permanently — chat.send returns started but no run executes, silently dropping messages

question: For Codex-backed WebChat sends, should Gateway keep returning `started` immediately, or should it delay/withhold `started` until the Codex dispatch path can prove turn startup or a safe forced rotation?
rationale: The code supports the failure class but the best repair changes a public chat-send liveness contract and may require maintainers to choose between compatibility, latency, recovery, and visibility.

options.title: Require runnable before `started`
options.body: Make `started` mean the send has reached a runnable dispatch path by force-rotating stale Codex threads or returning a visible error before ACK when that cannot be proven.

options.title: Keep immediate ACK with health recovery
options.body: Preserve the existing ACK timing but add health/audit state and visible post-ACK failures so users can recover wedged Codex threads without abandoning the session.

options.title: Wait for live repro first
options.body: Keep implementation paused until a current-main live or fixture replay of the oversized native-thread state identifies the narrowest failing boundary.

recommendation.title: Require runnable before `started`
recommendation.body: Make `started` mean the send has reached a runnable dispatch path by force-rotating stale Codex threads or returning a visible error before ACK when that cannot be proven.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the adjacent compaction recovery PR and follow-up hardening in the Codex overflow stack, making him the best available owner for the liveness-contract choice.
